BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in Paul's last letter: 'For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.' It is the noun for the departing itself — the breaking up of camp, the loosening of the ropes — and Paul uses it for his own death, already in sight.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for departure carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Paul's calm — the time of his departure at hand, and he is ready to be offered.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
